evidence: Quint. 1.6.26: cujus praeteritum perfectum et ulterius nōn invenītur
terms.comment: The completed past: lēgī, I read, have read (Traupman 226). Also tempus praeteritum perfectum (Traupman 248); in the perfect tense, tempore praeteritō perfectō (229).

phrases.latin: quod verbīs etiam accidit ut illī ferō, cujus praeteritum perfectum et ulterius nōn invenītur
phrases.english: which happens to verbs too, as to ferō, whose perfect and the tenses beyond it are not found

sources: Lewis & Short: praetereo · Lewis & Short: perficio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 226, 229, 244, 248.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
